objections.claim_attacked: hypothesis: a net merged during repair_timing explains the nonexistent net in the congestion report
objections.objection: The two stated hypotheses describe different mechanisms: povik says incremental groute mishandles merged nets (a routing-algorithm defect), while eder-matheus says the congestion heatmap was not updated when a net was deleted (a stale-report defect); the record never reconciles whether the net was merged into another (and thus still exists in some form) or deleted outright (and thus is absent), so the causal mechanism for the 'nonexistent net' is left ambiguous.

objections.claim_attacked: chosen_intervention: PR #7650 fixes the congestion issue
objections.objection: The record itself states that what PR #7650 changed — net merging, the report, or both — is not elaborated, and it separately lists a follow-up about updating the congestion report when a net is deleted; because the observation contains both a routing failure (GRT-0232/GRT-0116) and a report artifact (nonexistent-net marker), the record cannot establish whether PR #7650 addressed the routing failure, the stale marker, or both.

objections.claim_attacked: title: GRT congestion report references a nonexistent net
objections.objection: The title frames the incident as a reporting defect, but the observation says GRT fails with 'Routing congestion too high'; if the net does not exist, the record does not explain how GRT routes it and reports congestion, and it never establishes whether the routing failure and the nonexistent-net marker are the same underlying problem or two separate ones.

evidence_check: ASSERT — post_state is only the reporter's tentative 'sounds like it was resolved' with no numeric post-fix DRC, overflow, or runtime result and no confirmation the nonexistent-net marker is gone.
attribution_check: SUPPORTS — direct_quote names eder-matheus, gives a date (2025-06-25) and locator, and its text directly supports the chosen_intervention statement that PR #7650 fixes the congestion issue.
